newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: More criminal charges in CAM probe - CAD.
newsitem.headline: More criminal charges in CAM probe - CAD.

text.p: Singapore's Criminal Affairs Deparment (CAD) has levied further criminal charges against a former director and auditor of CAM International.
Ex-managing director and chief executive Raymond Chew was charged with 12 counts of falsifying of accounts, abetment of forgery and forgery, a CAD official told Reuters.
Cheong Khee San, an ex-auditor of the company, was charged on three counts for abetment of forgery.
Both men were offered bail of Singapore $300,000. A hearing has been set for August 29.
Chew had earlier been charged with criminal breach of trust for allegedly misappropriating S$1.45 million in company funds. He was offered bail of S$1.5 million in that case.
If convicted, Chew faces up to 10 years jail and a fine, or life imprisonment and a fine, according to the CAD.
CAD's charges follow a probe into the affairs of CAM after auditors Ernst & Young sent a report to the Ministry of Finance on April 29.
Precision engineering based CAM International is currently suspended from trade on the mainboard of the Singapore Stock Exchange.
